beats.say: A teenage girl in a small town called Nazareth. An ordinary day, until an angel stood before her.
Hail, thou that art highly favoured, the Lord is with thee: blessed art thou among women.
She would bear a son, and call his name Jesus. For with God nothing shall be impossible.
Behold the handmaid of the Lord; be it unto me according to thy word. Her yes changed the world. Yours matters too.
Mary hurried into the hill country to see her cousin Elisabeth, old and, against all hope, expecting a child.
When Elisabeth heard the salutation of Mary, the babe leaped in her womb.
Blessed art thou among women, and blessed is the fruit of thy womb.
And Mary sang: My soul doth magnify the Lord, And my spirit hath rejoiced in God my Saviour. Find someone to rejoice with.
Joseph was a carpenter, engaged to Mary. Then he learned she was with child, and it was not his.
He was a just man, and did not want to shame her. He planned to end it quietly. Then he slept.
Joseph, thou son of David, fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife: for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost.
Then Joseph being raised from sleep did as the angel had bidden him. Quiet obedience is a kind of courage too.
Simeon was an old man, just and devout, waiting all his life for the consolation of Israel.
One day a young couple carried their baby into the temple. And Simeon knew.
He took the child up in his arms, and blessed God, and said: Lord, now lettest thou thy servant depart in peace, according to thy word.
For mine eyes have seen thy salvation. A long wait, and it was worth every year. Keep watching.
Wise men from the east crossed a desert, following one star: Where is he that is born King of the Jews?
The star went before them, till it came and stood over where the young child was.
And they fell down, and worshipped him: and they presented unto him gifts; gold, and frankincense, and myrrh.
They travelled months to give him their best. What would it mean to bring him yours?
A jealous king wanted the child dead. And the angel warned Joseph in a dream.
Arise, and take the young child and his mother, and flee into Egypt: for Herod will seek the young child to destroy him.
When he arose, he took the young child and his mother by night, and departed into Egypt.
The Saviour of the world began life as a refugee. Whoever is far from home tonight, he knows the road.
John was baptizing crowds in the river Jordan. Then Jesus walked into the water, and John objected.
I have need to be baptized of thee, and comest thou to me? Jesus said: Suffer it to be so now.
And when he came up out of the water, lo, the heavens were opened, and he saw the Spirit of God descending like a dove.
This is my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased. Said before a single miracle. You are loved before you achieve anything.
Forty days alone in the desert, with no food. And when he was weakest, the tempter came.
If thou be the Son of God, command that these stones be made bread.
But he answered: It is written, Man shall not live by bread alone, but by every word that proceedeth out of the mouth of God.
He answered every lie with scripture, and angels came and ministered unto him. Know the words before the hungry days come.
Matthew collected taxes for Rome. Rich, and hated by his own people. Nobody expected anything good from him.
Jesus saw him sitting at the receipt of custom, and said unto him: Follow me. And he arose, and followed him.
That night Jesus ate at his house with publicans and sinners. Why eateth your Master with publicans and sinners?
They that be whole need not a physician, but they that are sick. If you feel too far gone, you are exactly who he came for.
Philip told Nathanael they had found the Messiah, from Nazareth. Can there any good thing come out of Nazareth?
Philip saith unto him: Come and see. Sometimes that is the whole argument.
Jesus said: Before that Philip called thee, when thou wast under the fig tree, I saw thee.
Rabbi, thou art the Son of God. One sentence: he had been seen, alone, before anyone knew. So have you.
A Roman officer, a commander of a hundred soldiers, came to a Jewish rabbi for help. His servant was dying.
Jesus offered to come. But the soldier said: Lord, I am not worthy that thou shouldest come under my roof: but speak the word only.
Jesus marvelled: I have not found so great faith, no, not in Israel.
And his servant was healed in the selfsame hour. Distance is no obstacle to him. Neither is the room you are in.
A foreign woman followed Jesus, crying: Have mercy on me, O Lord, thou Son of David; my daughter is grievously vexed.
But he answered her not a word. The disciples wanted her sent away. She kept asking.
Truth, Lord: yet the dogs eat of the crumbs which fall from their masters' table.
O woman, great is thy faith: be it unto thee even as thou wilt. Silence is not always no. Keep asking.
By a pool in Jerusalem lay a man which had an infirmity thirty and eight years.
Jesus asked him: Wilt thou be made whole? A strange question, for a man who had waited so long.
Sir, I have no man, when the water is troubled, to put me into the pool. Jesus said: Rise, take up thy bed, and walk.
And immediately the man was made whole. Thirty eight years, ended in a sentence. Your long wait is not too long for him.
A man blind from birth. The disciples asked: Who did sin, this man, or his parents?
Neither hath this man sinned, nor his parents: but that the works of God should be made manifest in him.
He made clay, anointed the man's eyes, and said: Go, wash in the pool of Siloam. He went his way, and washed, and came seeing.
The leaders interrogated him. He said: One thing I know, that, whereas I was blind, now I see. Your story is enough.
They brought Jesus a man that was deaf, and had an impediment in his speech. A whole life of silence.
He took him aside from the multitude, away from the staring crowd, and put his fingers into his ears.
And looking up to heaven, he sighed, and saith unto him: Ephphatha, that is, Be opened.
And straightway his ears were opened. He hath done all things well. He still takes people aside, one at a time.
On the sabbath, in the synagogue, there was a man which had a withered hand. And they watched Jesus, to accuse him.
Is it lawful to do good on the sabbath days, or to do evil? to save life, or to kill? But they held their peace.
He said unto the man: Stretch forth thine hand. And he stretched it out: and his hand was restored whole as the other.
Rules can become a reason not to help. Jesus never let them. Who is the person you have been waiting to help?
Among the tombs lived a man no chain could hold, crying day and night, and cutting himself with stones.
Jesus asked his name. My name is Legion: for we are many.
The spirits fled into a herd of swine, and the herd ran violently down a steep place into the sea.
They found him sitting, clothed, and in his right mind. Go home to thy friends, and tell them how great things the Lord hath done for thee.
The tax collectors cornered Peter: Doth not your master pay tribute? Peter said yes, without asking.
Jesus said: Go thou to the sea, and cast an hook, and take up the fish that first cometh up.
When thou hast opened his mouth, thou shalt find a piece of money: that take, and give unto them for me and thee.
For me and thee. He paid what Peter owed alongside his own. He still pays debts we cannot.
Jesus took Peter, James and John up an high mountain apart. And he was transfigured before them.
His face did shine as the sun, and his raiment was white as the light.
A voice out of the cloud: This is my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased; hear ye him. And they fell on their faces.
Jesus touched them: Arise, and be not afraid. They saw no man, save Jesus only. When the glory fades, he is still there.

title: He Took Her by the Hand

beats.say: After the synagogue, Jesus went to Peter's house. Simon's wife's mother lay sick of a fever.
And he came and took her by the hand, and lifted her up; and immediately the fever left her.
And she ministered unto them. Healed, and straight back to serving the people she loved.
By sunset, all the city was gathered together at the door. One kitchen became a hospital. Your home can be a door too.
A young man ran to Jesus and knelt: Good Master, what shall I do that I may inherit eternal life?
He had kept every commandment from his youth. Then Jesus beholding him loved him.
One thing thou lackest: go thy way, sell whatsoever thou hast, and give to the poor, and come, take up the cross, and follow me.
And he went away grieved: for he had great possessions. Love asked for everything. What are you holding too tightly?
A servant owed his king ten thousand talents, more than he could earn in a thousand lifetimes. He begged: Have patience with me.
The lord was moved with compassion, and loosed him, and forgave him the debt. All of it.
Then he found a fellowservant who owed him an hundred pence, took him by the throat, and said: Pay me that thou owest.
Shouldest not thou also have had compassion on thy fellowservant, even as I had pity on thee? Remember what you were forgiven.
A householder went out early in the morning to hire labourers into his vineyard, for a penny a day.
At the eleventh hour he found more: Why stand ye here all the day idle? Because no man hath hired us.
At evening, the last hired received a full penny. The first expected more, and received the same.
Is thine eye evil, because I am good? So the last shall be first, and the first last. Grace is never late, and never fair. Thank God.
A certain man made a great supper, and bade many. And they all with one consent began to make excuse.
A field to see. Oxen to try. A new marriage. Everyone was busy.
Go out quickly into the streets and lanes of the city, and bring in hither the poor, and the maimed, and the halt, and the blind.
Go out into the highways and hedges, and compel them to come in, that my house may be filled. There is still a seat with your name.
Twelve years old. His parents travelled a whole day home from Jerusalem before they realised he was missing.
After three days they found him in the temple, sitting in the midst of the doctors, both hearing them, and asking them questions.
Son, why hast thou thus dealt with us? How is it that ye sought me? wist ye not that I must be about my Father's business?
And Jesus increased in wisdom and stature, and in favour with God and man. Growing up is holy work too.
Jesus told this parable to the end that men ought always to pray, and not to faint.
There was a judge, which feared not God, neither regarded man. And a widow came to him, saying: Avenge me of mine adversary.
He refused. She came back. And back again. Until he said: lest by her continual coming she weary me.
And shall not God avenge his own elect, which cry day and night unto him? If an unjust judge gives in, how much more your Father.
Midnight. A friend has arrived from a journey, and the cupboard is empty. So you knock next door: Friend, lend me three loaves.
Trouble me not: the door is now shut, and my children are with me in bed.
But because of his importunity he will rise and give him as many as he needeth. Persistence opened the door.
Ask, and it shall be given you; seek, and ye shall find; knock, and it shall be opened unto you. So keep knocking.
A man ploughing a field struck something hard. Treasure, hid in a field.
And for joy thereof goeth and selleth all that he hath, and buyeth that field.
A merchant, seeking goodly pearls, found one pearl of great price, went and sold all that he had, and bought it.
Neither man felt he was losing anything. That is the kingdom of heaven: worth everything, and found with joy.
A farmer sowed good seed in his field. But while men slept, his enemy came and sowed tares among the wheat.
When the blade sprung up, the servants saw weeds everywhere. An enemy hath done this. Shall we pull them up?
Nay; lest while ye gather up the tares, ye root up also the wheat with them. Let both grow together until the harvest.
Not every judgment is ours to make, and not today. Tend your own wheat. The harvest belongs to God.
A certain man had two sons; and he came to the first, and said: Son, go work to day in my vineyard.
He answered and said: I will not. But afterward he repented, and went.
The second said: I go, sir. And went not.
Which of the two did the will of his father? A late yes beats an empty one. It is not too late to go.
Jesus described the end of all things: all nations gathered before him, divided as a shepherd divideth his sheep from the goats.
For I was an hungred, and ye gave me meat: I was thirsty, and ye gave me drink: I was a stranger, and ye took me in.
I was sick, and ye visited me: I was in prison, and ye came unto me. And they asked: Lord, when saw we thee?
Inasmuch as ye have done it unto one of the least of these my brethren, ye have done it unto me. He hides in plain sight.
To fishermen and farmers on a hillside, Jesus said: Ye are the salt of the earth. Ye are the light of the world.
A city that is set on an hill cannot be hid.
Neither do men light a candle, and put it under a bushel, but on a candlestick; and it giveth light unto all that are in the house.
Let your light so shine before men, that they may see your good works, and glorify your Father which is in heaven. Do not hide it.
Ye have heard that it hath been said, Thou shalt love thy neighbour, and hate thine enemy.
But I say unto you, Love your enemies, bless them that curse you, do good to them that hate you, and pray for them which despitefully use you.
For he maketh his sun to rise on the evil and on the good, and sendeth rain on the just and on the unjust.
Not the feeling first. The prayer first. Say one name tonight, the hardest one, and ask God to bless them.
Peter thought he was being generous: Lord, how oft shall my brother sin against me, and I forgive him? till seven times?
Jesus saith unto him: I say not unto thee, Until seven times: but, Until seventy times seven.
Not a number to count to. A way to live. Forgiveness that stops keeping score.
It does not mean what happened was fine. It means the debt is handed to God. Hand him one tonight.
Thy King cometh unto thee, meek, and sitting upon an ass. Not a warhorse. A donkey.
A very great multitude spread their garments in the way; others cut down branches from the trees, and strawed them in the way.
Hosanna to the Son of David: Blessed is he that cometh in the name of the Lord; Hosanna in the highest.
And when he beheld the city, he wept over it. The same crowd would shout crucify within a week. He came anyway.
The last supper. No servant to wash the dusty feet. So Jesus rose, took a towel, and poured water into a basin.
Peter protested: Lord, dost thou wash my feet? Thou shalt never wash my feet.
Jesus answered him: If I wash thee not, thou hast no part with me.
If I then, your Lord and Master, have washed your feet; ye also ought to wash one another's feet. Greatness looks like a towel.
Torches in the garden at midnight. Soldiers, and at their head, one of the twelve.
Judas drew near unto Jesus to kiss him. But Jesus said unto him: Judas, betrayest thou the Son of man with a kiss?
Peter drew a sword and struck a servant. Jesus said: Put up again thy sword. And he touched his ear, and healed him.
Betrayed by a friend, and still healing his enemy. If someone close has wounded you, he knows that kiss.
At dawn they brought Jesus to Pilate, the Roman governor. Art thou the King of the Jews?
Jesus answered: My kingdom is not of this world. To this end was I born, that I should bear witness unto the truth.
Pilate saith unto him: What is truth? And he walked out without waiting for an answer.
The answer was standing in front of him. I am the way, the truth, and the life. Do not walk out before you hear it.
A visitor from Africa named Simon, coming into Jerusalem from the country, minding his own business.
Jesus had fallen under the weight. So they laid hold upon Simon, and on him they laid the cross, that he might bear it after Jesus.
He walked the road to Golgotha behind Jesus, carrying what Jesus carried.
Mark remembers his sons by name, Alexander and Rufus. One unplanned day became his family's story. Take up thy cross, and follow.
When the sixth hour was come, there was darkness over the whole land until the ninth hour.
And Jesus cried with a loud voice, and gave up the ghost. And the veil of the temple was rent in twain from the top to the bottom.
A Roman centurion had watched it all. He had seen many men die. Never one like this.
Truly this man was the Son of God. The first to say it at the cross was an outsider. There is no one he cannot reach.
Sunday, before sunrise. Two women walking to a sealed tomb, wondering who would move the stone.
There was a great earthquake: for the angel of the Lord descended from heaven, and came and rolled back the stone.
He is not here: for he is risen, as he said. Come, see the place where the Lord lay.
And they departed quickly with fear and great joy. Both at once. That is what Easter feels like.
Mary stood without at the sepulchre weeping. They have taken away my Lord, and I know not where they have laid him.
Someone behind her asked: Woman, why weepest thou? whom seekest thou? She, supposing him to be the gardener, did not look up.
Jesus saith unto her: Mary. She turned herself, and saith unto him: Rabboni; which is to say, Master.
She ran to the disciples: I have seen the Lord. He knows your name too, and he says it the same way.
After everything, Peter went back to what he knew: I go a fishing. And that night they caught nothing.
When the morning was now come, Jesus stood on the shore: but the disciples knew not that it was Jesus.
John said: It is the Lord. And on the shore they saw a fire of coals, and fish laid thereon, and bread.
Jesus saith unto them: Come and dine. After their failure, breakfast. He still makes room at the fire for you.
The eleven disciples went away into Galilee, into a mountain. They worshipped him: but some doubted.
He gave the work to worshippers and doubters alike. All power is given unto me in heaven and in earth.
Go ye therefore, and teach all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Ghost.
And, lo, I am with you alway, even unto the end of the world. Amen. Doubts and all, you are sent, and not alone.
Forty days after the resurrection, Jesus led them out to the Mount of Olives. Ye shall receive power, and ye shall be witnesses unto me.
And while they beheld, he was taken up; and a cloud received him out of their sight.
Two men stood by them in white apparel: Ye men of Galilee, why stand ye gazing up into heaven?
This same Jesus shall so come in like manner. Until then, there is work to do. Stop staring at the sky. Go.

title: She Hath Done What She Could

beats.say: Days before the cross, a woman came having an alabaster box of ointment of spikenard very precious. A year's wages.
She brake the box, and poured it on his head. Some had indignation: Why was this waste of the ointment made?
Jesus said: Let her alone. She hath wrought a good work on me. She hath done what she could.
Wheresoever this gospel shall be preached, this also that she hath done shall be spoken of. Love that looks wasteful is never wasted.
A dinner at a Pharisee's house. Then a woman everyone knew as a sinner walked in, uninvited.
She stood at his feet behind him weeping, and began to wash his feet with tears, and did wipe them with the hairs of her head.
The host thought: This man, if he were a prophet, would have known who and what manner of woman this is.
Her sins, which are many, are forgiven; for she loved much. Thy faith hath saved thee; go in peace. He knew exactly who she was.
In the synagogue was a woman bowed together for eighteen years. She could in no wise lift up herself.
Eighteen years of looking at the ground. Then Jesus saw her, and called her to him.
Woman, thou art loosed from thine infirmity. And he laid his hands on her: and immediately she was made straight, and glorified God.
Whatever has bent you over for years, he sees it. He can still say: thou art loosed. Look up.
When the wolf comes, the hired hand runs. He seeth the wolf coming, and leaveth the sheep, and fleeth.
I am the good shepherd: the good shepherd giveth his life for the sheep.
My sheep hear my voice, and I know them, and they follow me.
Neither shall any man pluck them out of my hand. You are not too lost, and not too far, to be carried home.

title: Whom Say Ye That I Am?

beats.say: On a road far from Jerusalem, Jesus asked his friends: Whom do men say that I the Son of man am?
A prophet, they said. Elijah. John the Baptist, back from the dead. Everyone had an opinion.
Then he made it personal: But whom say ye that I am? And Peter answered: Thou art the Christ, the Son of the living God.
Flesh and blood hath not revealed it unto thee, but my Father which is in heaven. The question still stands. Whom say ye?
